Alright, let me think through this year on my land.

---

**My situation this year**

I'm 58, been on this land since I was a young man. My two sons are grown — the older one works in the city at a factory, sends money home. My wife and I handle most of the farm work, and my daughter-in-law helps when the stevia needs picking. I have 30 mu — that's not small but not big either. Enough to feed us and have something to sell, but I watch every yuan.

I split the land the way I've done for a few years now: **25 mu goes to wheat-maize double crop** — winter wheat comes off in June, maize goes straight in. That's how we do it in this village, everybody does. **5 mu I keep for stevia** (甜叶菊). My neighbor Old Wang started with it maybe eight years ago, the company sends people to buy the leaves, price is okay. Stevia makes more money per mu than grain but it's hard on the back — lots of picking.

---

**Wheat (25 mu) — planted last October, comes off this June**

I put this in already in October. I buy regular seed from the co-op, nothing fancy — the hybrid wheat seed is expensive and I don't see my neighbors getting much more yield with it. Used about 15 kg of seed per mu, drilled in rows.

Before planting I spread two bags of the compound fertilizer — that 15-15-15 stuff, each bag is 50 jin (25 kg), so two bags per mu. That's the base. Then in spring, around Qingming when the wheat is greening up, I'll go out with urea — one bag per mu, maybe 15 kg. If it looks yellow I add a bit more at jointing, but usually one topdress is enough.

Water — I watered once before winter (it was dry in November). This spring I'll water at greening, then again at grain filling in May. So three waterings in total if the rain comes normal. The well pump costs electricity, about 30-40 yuan per mu each time, adds up.

Spray — I'll put on the herbicide once in spring for the broadleaf weeds. If I see aphids later I'll spray once more but usually don't need to.

Last year I got 420 kg per mu. This year should be similar if the spring rain comes. I'm hoping for 450.

---

**Maize (25 mu) — goes in right after wheat in mid-June**

This is the tight time of year. Wheat combine comes, within a week I've got to get the maize in. I hire the planter — the man down the road has the machine, charges 30 yuan per mu and does the seed and base fertilizer at the same time.

I use the hybrid seed, Zhengdan or whatever the co-op has that year — about 2.5 kg per mu, costs maybe 40 yuan. Base fertilizer goes in with the seed, I use 40 kg of the compound per mu. When the maize is about knee-high, around late July, I topdress urea, about 15 kg per mu. That's the "big mouth stage" — the corn is hungry then.

If the summer rain is normal I don't water at all. If it's dry at tasseling I'll give it one water. Last year we had a dry August and I watered twice — cost me but the ears filled out.

For spray — herbicide after planting before the maize comes up, that's it usually. Sometimes armyworm but not every year.

Last year I got about 520 kg per mu. Good year.

---

**Stevia (5 mu) — transplant seedlings late April**

This is different from the grain. The company sends the seedlings, I transplant them by hand — that's a lot of work, my wife and I and sometimes we hire two women from the village for two days. Goes in around April 20.

Stevia wants more fertilizer and more water than wheat. I put compound fertilizer at about 60 kg per mu before transplanting, then urea twice during the summer, maybe 10 kg each time. It also likes potash, so I add a half-bag of potassium sulfate. Costs more — maybe 250 yuan per mu for fertilizer alone.

Water — I irrigate maybe 4 or 5 times through the summer. It doesn't like dry weather, the leaves get small.

The big work is harvesting. We cut the plant two or three times through the season, strip the leaves, dry them. My daughter-in-law helps. If we can't keep up we hire help — 80 yuan per person per day.

Company pays by weight of dried leaves. Last year I got about 350 kg dried per mu, came to maybe 2,500 yuan per mu. Good money but hard work.

---

**What I'm worried about**

Spring rain. If April is dry I'll have to pump extra for the wheat, costs more. Fertilizer prices went up again last year — I'm using the same amount but paying more. And my back isn't what it was at 40, the stevia picking is getting harder each year. If my daughter-in-law takes a factory job I might have to cut stevia back.
